cells.tense: Something is ready to begin, and the first piece of it is in your hand.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Find where someone's share runs lower than it should, and put your help behind it until the work is done — one place, finished, this week.
cells.core:
Something is ready to begin and the first piece of it is already in your hand. What lets it go anywhere is the fairness underneath — nobody carrying more than their part, the work spread so it holds when one person rests. You read that spread quickly, and you're usually the one making the small adjustments that keep it true.

Your strength is meant to move outward here. Pick a place where someone has less than they should, and give a finished piece of help — whole, not a gesture. Not every place. One, done. Resources flow back to you because the first thing stayed fair while you were building it.
cells.sheetLine: Fairness is what lets the first thing hold.
cells.verb: holding the first material of something not yet made
cells.place: at the balance where what is given and what is owed are weighed

cells.tense: You'll be correcting shares on a thing that hasn't even started yet.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Take a page and write what you actually feel about this beginning — all of it, nothing crossed out. Read it and stop.
cells.core:
Every scale is set before anything has been put on them. Who owes what, where this will go unfair later — the corrections run on before the actual start, and the beginning keeps waiting while the arithmetic finishes. You're bracing for a breakdown in the split that hasn't happened. The people who'd be building it alongside you can feel the scale being checked on them.

Get the whole of it down on one page — every feeling about this starting, none of it crossed out — and read it without fixing any of it. Nothing turns final when you do that; knowing it keeps widening. The accounting quiets once the whole thing is allowed to sit there at once. What's left after you read it is usually where the beginning actually is.
cells.sheetLine: You're weighing a thing that hasn't started.
cells.verb: holding the first material of something not yet made
cells.place: at the balance where what is given and what is owed are weighed

cells.tense: The first piece was there to pick up, and it's still sitting where it was.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Spread out what this beginning takes — what it needs, what you'd hold, who's in it. Sit with it until you've seen every part.
cells.core:
You're standing at a door you've already passed. The offering came, the first piece was in reach, and it wasn't taken. The sense of proportion you're good at turned inward instead — you've been the one absorbing the short end of an arrangement, and nobody has re-weighed it since. Balance is meant to bring what's out of proportion back, and here the thing out of proportion is the last one anyone adjusts.

Seeing the whole shape of it is the move that asks nothing of what's empty. Lay it all out — what it requires, the work, the others involved — until there's nothing left unseen, and the true size of the thing turns up. It usually ends on a plain fact about what starting would require. That fact is usable. It's a place to stand even if the timing has gone.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying the uneven share nobody has re-weighed.
cells.verb: holding the first material of something not yet made
cells.place: at the balance where what is given and what is owed are weighed

cells.tense: You're the hand on the scale, and your own name for it is that nothing happened.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: Take one arrangement you've been quietly keeping fair and look at it plainly until you can see what you did to hold it. That one, nothing else.
cells.core:
Things around you come back into proportion, and the one doing it says it just worked out that way. A gap gets covered, a weight gets shifted back where it belongs, and the balance is yours — you've not said so, not even to yourself. The person on the better end of it gets the correction, and you get the story that there was no correction to make. The work is real and it stays unowned.

Look at a single arrangement you've been holding fair, and see the whole of what you did — the choice, the piece you protected, all of it, nothing hidden. Nobody needs to hear about it, and nothing about how you act has to change. Looking is the act. Once the hand is yours on purpose, the next balance you set is one you chose.
cells.sheetLine: The balance in this is yours and you call it luck.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that another person needs this person's help right now; the record gives the capacity to offer support, not a recipient waiting. A reader could reasonably say nobody around them needs anything, so the ask is written as an offer that gives them the right to pick where it lands, and it survives being wrong. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the closing move about seeing a share at the end without having looked; I cut it.
